facts.claim: The central issue is regional transport availability, not a demonstrated national supply or demand loss. Planned outages create conditional capacity shortfalls across several TGP zones, while the missing regional supply, demand, measured-flow, and rerouting denominator prevents estimating a national balance share. [km_tgp_notice_detail:1787932505364330000:46485bb248300193468625e90e1a0552f36c4adb8a4d2cdff1a507c289e82063,km_tgp_segment_capacity:1788105216817246000:a4457f5a9ca6180e2bb5e83f4fab842ac9a9ac3f88e3d9819ba77215daf9490d]

Inventory context is above recent norms: Lower 48 working gas was 3,184 Bcf, 5.5% above the five-year average; East storage was 727 Bcf, 5.1% above average; South Central storage was 1,061 Bcf, 3.0% above average. This is regional and system context, not attribution to any TGP event. [eia_wngsr:1788115874039669000:c7dd258cb0915a825acbed60129cdeb5e37aaf8e0ebe0021c97414369d461469]

The authoritative change ledger identifies a worsened forecast at Segment 530 BH: operating capacity was revised from 1.55 million to 905,000 Dth/day, a 645,000 Dth/day (41.6%) decrease, for changed periods from September 7 through October 11. [km_tgp_notice_detail:1787932512717694000:4e5308a6b60198988cebfe87c90c7936ec29248dea254a2e2949d8b71262ebc6,km_tgp_notice_detail:1787932505364330000:46485bb248300193468625e90e1a0552f36c4adb8a4d2cdff1a507c289e82063]

The same ledger identifies improved forecast capacity at Segment 245 FH: 970,000 Dth/day versus 680,000 Dth/day previously, an increase of 290,000 Dth/day for September 21–27. [km_tgp_notice_detail:1787932512717694000:4e5308a6b60198988cebfe87c90c7936ec29248dea254a2e2949d8b71262ebc6,km_tgp_notice_detail:1787932505364330000:46485bb248300193468625e90e1a0552f36c4adb8a4d2cdff1a507c289e82063]

glossary.definition: The difference between gas prices at two locations, often reflecting transport constraints and local supply-demand conditions.
Pipeline transport capacity that is available for scheduling; it is not measured physical gas flow.
A calculated gap between a captured scheduled quantity and forecast operating capacity, assuming the schedule does not change. It is not a confirmed curtailment.

headline: Transport constraints are the key watch: storage is above recent norms, but planned TGP capacity reductions could tighten regional routing if scheduled volumes persist.
missing_data: Regional basis-price observations and an exact TGP leg-to-contract mapping.
Weather, production, measured-flow, and futures observations.
Point-in-time regional supply, demand, and rerouting volumes needed to size any national supply/demand share.
Future nominations and rerouting that would confirm or eliminate conditional shortfalls.
Detail text and capacity confirmation for the August 28 and August 29 restriction notices. [km_tgp_critical:1788110122419257000:5c924dc6c23dab467c649f8808dc8af00af0e929cc7dc5c389521b9eec637518]
plain_english_summary: Storage is moderately above normal, which argues against inferring a broad shortage. The investable question is instead whether planned reductions leave too little transport room on particular TGP legs. That remains conditional because future schedules and rerouting are unknown, and no regional price evidence is available.

watch_items.scenario: For September 14–20, Station 860 (segment 548 BH, Zone 1) has an 868,000 Dth/day gross planned reduction to 725,000 Dth/day. If the August 30 captured schedule of 1,393,684 Dth/day were unchanged, the calculated conditional shortfall is 668,684 Dth/day. This could raise regional transport scarcity, but it is not a price prediction or confirmed curtailment.
watch_items.title: Station 860 BH: largest conditional shortfall

watch_items.scenario: Current notices signal operational restrictions and an emergent repair around Segment 860 BH. They may constrain incremental scheduling, but the available evidence does not establish a lasting operating-capacity reduction or a regional price effect.
watch_items.title: Current restriction notices require confirmation

why_it_matters: Planned reductions may matter through regional basis and transport availability if they bind against persistent schedules. The evidence does not support a national Henry Hub price call: no regional price, physical-flow, production, weather, or futures observations are available, and inventory is above recent norms.
